top_signals.title: Southeast Asia Keeps Building Gas Plants Despite Hormuz LNG Shock
top_signals.summary: Countries in Southeast Asia are still building natural gas-fired power plants despite the price inflation in gas caused by the Middle East war. Asian countries are also building more LNG import capacity, Global Energy Monitor reported. top_signals.title: Saudi Arabia Sells 100 Million Barrels of Crude to Asia via Hormuz
top_signals.summary: Saudi Arabia has sold almost 100 million barrels of crude to Asian buyers via the Strait of Hormuz since the middle of last week, when it pivoted to the chokepoint it wanted to avoid with the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea. With the pipeline out of service, the Kingdom has sold 100 million barrels of crude, which is roughly one day of total global oil demand, to Asian buyers for October and November delivery through the Strait of Hormuz, trade sources with knowledge of the deals told Bloomberg on Thursday. top_signals.title: US Jobless Claims Hover Close to Historic Lows at 197,000
top_signals.summary: Applications for US unemployment benefits fell to the lowest level since July, edging down 1,000 to 197,000 in the week ended Sept. 19, according to Labor Department data released Thursday. Enda Curran reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
